title: Regenerate functional human teeth in congenital tooth agenesis

concept.text: Induce development and eruption of missing permanent teeth with usable structure and occlusion. TRG035 entered human safety testing, but permission to run a trial is not approval of a tooth-regeneration treatment or proof of human regrowth. Proposed completion test: PMDA/MHLW or equivalent marketing authorization supported by controlled human evidence of new permanent-tooth formation and eruption, functional occlusion, and at least two years of dental safety and durability follow-up. Test set by: Proposed editorial clinical test; Japanese regulators would determine authorization. The first registered trial's primary endpoint is safety, not tooth regeneration. Overlaps: BME-11, PHA-12. Sources given: [Japanese official TRG035 trial registry](https://rctportal.mhlw.go.jp/en/detail?trial_id=jRCT2051240154) ; [Kitano Hospital explanation of the clinical programme](https://www.kitano-hp.or.jp/english/info/20240503?style=whats-new).

page.title: Tooth regeneration for congenital tooth agenesis
page.definition: A treatment causes a permanent tooth to develop where it was congenitally absent. One investigational approach blocks USAG-1, a protein that suppresses tooth development, so that a dormant tooth bud can resume growth. A bud visible on an image is an early stage. The clinical goal is a tooth that emerges through the gum and meets an opposing tooth during biting and chewing.

goal.need: In a Japanese dental-clinic survey, 1,568 of 15,544 children lacked at least one permanent tooth other than a wisdom tooth. Japan has an estimated 10,240 children in the proposed treatment population for severe agenesis. Missing teeth can make chewing and speaking difficult. Dentures can help children chew, but may need adjustment or replacement as their jaws grow. If a new tooth erupts and meets an opposing tooth, a child could chew with their own tooth in that space.

completion.title: MHLW grants marketing approval for a tooth-regeneration treatment for congenital tooth agenesis.
completion.criterion: Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare grants product-specific marketing approval for treating congenital tooth agenesis through regeneration of missing permanent teeth, following review of the product's quality, efficacy and safety. The application must provide sufficient supporting evidence from ethical, scientific and reliable data. The regulator determines the indication-specific evidence required.
completion.set_by: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, Approval Applications for Drugs, Section 1, paragraph 1, implementing Article 14; revision dated 9 October 2024.
completion.threshold_quote: Minister of Health, Labour and Welfare shall grant approval for each product based on the review.
completion.basis: Japanese marketing approval establishes which product may be used for which indication after review of quality, efficacy and safety. The general rule leaves tooth-specific endpoints and follow-up to the indication-specific review. Orphan-drug designation identifies a proposed indication during development.

milestones.title: Normal third upper molars form in mice whose tooth development is genetically arrested.
milestones.criterion: Histological sections taken immediately after birth show normal third upper molars in mice lacking both Msx1 and Usag-1. The comparison is with newborn mice lacking Msx1 alone.
milestones.set_by: Murashima-Suginami and colleagues, published genetic-rescue experiment in Science Advances, Figure 1; this test concerns a mouse model.
milestones.threshold_quote: all USAG-1−/−/Msx1−/− mice had normal third maxillary molar teeth

milestones.title: Nonclinical findings support a tooth-regeneration drug's proposed human dose and exposure duration.
milestones.criterion: Before the first human study, nonclinical findings for the candidate drug must support both the proposed starting dose in humans and the planned duration of exposure.
milestones.set_by: International Council for Harmonisation, ICH E8(R1), section 4.2; a general drug-development requirement applied here to tooth regeneration.
milestones.threshold_quote: sufficient non-clinical information to support initial human doses and duration of exposure.

milestones.title: TRG035 completes its registered Phase I single-dose safety study in adults.
milestones.criterion: Complete the primary safety assessment in jRCT2051240154, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study targeting 30 healthy men aged 30 to under 65 with at least one missing molar. Each participant receives one intravenous dose of TRG035 or placebo. The five TRG035 dose levels are 0.4, 1.2, 4.0, 12.0 and 24.0 mg/kg.
milestones.set_by: TRG035 study investigators, registered Phase I protocol jRCT2051240154; its primary endpoint is safety, without a publicly specified numerical safety pass criterion.

milestones.title: Treatment induces a missing permanent tooth to form in a person with congenital tooth agenesis.
milestones.criterion: Document congenital absence of a permanent tooth at a specified site before treatment and subsequent formation of a permanent tooth at that site in at least one treated patient.
milestones.set_by: Atlas minimum for human proof of concept. No external body was found to define one patient as a sufficient success threshold for TR-002.

milestones.title: Confirmatory studies establish safety and efficacy of tooth regeneration in the intended patient population.
milestones.criterion: Confirmatory clinical studies establish safety and efficacy for the intended indication and patient population and provide an adequate basis for marketing approval. Their endpoints must be clinically relevant measures of disease burden or adequate surrogates for predicting the burden or consequences of disease.
milestones.set_by: International Council for Harmonisation, ICH E8(R1), section 4.3.2; the general confirmatory-evidence standard, without a published tooth-regeneration protocol.
milestones.threshold_quote: safe and effective for use for the intended indication and recipient population.

milestones.title: An extra upper incisor erupts in a mouse lacking USAG-1.
milestones.criterion: Examination of the dentition identifies an erupted incisor in excess of the normal number in the upper jaw of a USAG-1-deficient mouse.
milestones.set_by: Murashima-Suginami and colleagues, published mouse dentition study, 2007.
milestones.threshold_quote: Rudiment incisors survive and erupt as supernumerary teeth as a result of USAG-1 abrogation

milestones.title: An anti-USAG-1 antibody reduces the frequency of missing lower molars in EDA1-deficient mice.
milestones.criterion: After pregnant mice receive a USAG-1-neutralizing antibody on embryonic day 13, examine the lower jaws of EDA1-deficient offspring at five weeks. A smaller proportion of treated offspring than controls must have missing lower molars.
milestones.set_by: Murashima-Suginami and colleagues, antibody experiment in Science Advances, Figure 3 and Methods.
milestones.threshold_quote: rescued molar hypodontia in the mandible of EDA1−/− mice compared with control mice

not_found: No tooth-specific regulatory or society threshold for eruption rate, functional occlusion or durability was found.
No peer-reviewed human tooth-regeneration efficacy results or detailed Phase I safety results for TRG035 were found.
No animal sample sizes or numerical acceptance limits for TRG035's completed regulatory nonclinical studies were located.
A prespecified numerical efficacy success criterion for TR-002 could not be verified in the Japanese trial registries or sponsor documents.
No regulator or dental society statement disputing the feasibility or value of regeneration for congenital tooth agenesis was identified.

case_label = "Severity". Reason: Severity identifies the distinction the clinical programme uses to define its initial patient population and a possible expansion.

definition = "A treatment causes a permanent tooth to develop where it was congenitally absent. One investigational approach blocks USAG-1, a protein that suppresses tooth development, so that a dormant tooth bud can resume growth. A bud visible on an image is an early stage. The clinical goal is a tooth that emerges through the gum and meets an opposing tooth during biting and chewing.". Reason: The definition gains a biological explanation of how a tooth could form and distinguishes an early finding on imaging from a tooth that functions in the bite.

goal.need = "In a Japanese dental-clinic survey, 1,568 of 15,544 children lacked at least one permanent tooth other than a wisdom tooth. Japan has an estimated 10,240 children in the proposed treatment population for severe agenesis. Missing teeth can make chewing and speaking difficult. Dentures can help children chew, but may need adjustment or replacement as their jaws grow. If a new tooth erupts and meets an opposing tooth, a child could chew with their own tooth in that space.". Reason: The clinic survey gives the frequency of agenesis among patients but leaves out the size of the severe treatment population and what regeneration could change for a growing child.
